subject: MSA / Order Form — arbitration safeguards & injunction procedure
summary: Coordination between sales, legal, and contracts on Meridian's redlines for governing law, arbitration carveouts for injunctive relief, and venue preferences. Finalizing fallback language and confirming sign-off path for Order Form execution.
messages:
From: Emma Lyons <emma.lyons@meridianhealth.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.com
Cc: legal@meridianhealth.com
Date: Wed, 15 Aug 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MSA redlines — provisional remedies / jurisdiction

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Meridian's legal team returned a marked MSA (attached) with three principal asks that we need Redwood's help on:

1) Governing law — they prefer our contracts governed by New York law rather than California (they cite parent comp statutes).
2) Arbitration — they want broader arbitration for commercial disputes but an express carveout for "provisional, injunctive and emergency relief" to remain with the courts.
3) Venue / service — they also want a local (NY) venue and an expedited notice period for injunctive actions.

They attached Meridian_MSA_redlines_v3.docx and asked if Redwood can propose narrow language that preserves your arbitration program while giving them comfort on emergency relief.

Can you loop in legal/ops and let me know the quickest path to an agreement here? We're on a fairly tight procurement timeline — they want a signed Order Form before month end.

Best,
Emma
Director, Strategic Sourcing
Meridian Health

Attachments: Meridian_MSA_redlines_v3.docx (docx, 120KB)

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com
Cc: emma.lyons@meridianhealth.com
Date: Wed, 15 Aug 2028 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA redlines — provisional remedies / jurisdiction

Team — forwarding Meridian's redline. Key asks summarized above. Quick thoughts:

- Governing law: NY is acceptable if we preserve a Delaware forum selection for actions seeking statutory relief tied to corporate operations; but we prefer CA/Del preference for predictability. Laura, do we have precedent for pure NY choice?
- Arbitration carveout: We typically allow injunctive relief carveouts but need to limit to narrow equitable relief (temporary restraining orders, preliminary injunctions) and add an emergency escalation path so we can route to our emergency on-call infra if needed.
- Venue: Meridian wants NY; acceptable if arbitration remains in NY or AAA/ICC as fallback.

Action items: Laura — can you draft compact fallback language (3-4 sentences) that: (a) keeps general disputes in arbitration, (b) permits courts to grant provisional injunctive relief, and (c) confirms expedited notice and meet-and-confer prior to emergency filings unless irreparable harm exists?
Marcus — please check whether Order Form signing timeline can be shifted by one week if we need one more internal review.
Karthik — I'll need sales cover language to set internal expectations for procurement timelines and commercial concessions (credits or SOW carveouts).

Emma — we'll aim to circulate draft language within 24 hours.

Thanks,
Olga
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Chris Patel <chris.patel@meridianhealth.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Cc: emma.lyons@meridianhealth.com, legal@meridianhealth.com
Date: Thu, 16 Aug 2028 08:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA redlines — provisional remedies / jurisdiction

Thanks for the quick response. A few clarifications from our counsel:

- The carveout must explicitly state that Meridian can seek injunctive or other provisional relief in any court of competent jurisdiction to prevent immediate, irreparable harm — they will not agree to be forced into arbitration first for those remedies.
- They prefer governing law = New York. If Redwood insists on CA/Del, Meridian will ask for express waiver language around forum non conveniens defenses.
- Timing: they need a signed Order Form by 08/31 to align with their budget cycle.

We're open to those 3-4 sentence proposals you mentioned; the faster we get it, the better. Also attaching a tracker with the key procurement milestones.

Regards,
Chris
Sr. Contracts Manager, Meridian Health

Attachments: ProvisionalRelief_Tracker.xlsx (xlsx, 45KB)

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com
Cc: emma.lyons@meridianhealth.com
Date: Thu, 16 Aug 2028 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA redlines — provisional remedies / jurisdiction

Folks — drafting note and proposed text below. Kept it intentionally tight to address Meridian's concerns while preserving our arbitration program. Please review and flag anything you can't live with.

Proposed insertion (Order Form / MSA — Dispute Resolution):
"Notwithstanding the Parties' agreement to resolve disputes through binding arbitration under Section X, either Party may seek from any court of competent jurisdiction provisional, injunctive, or other equitable relief to the extent necessary to preserve the status quo, prevent irreparable harm, or protect the confidentiality or safety of data or systems. Such relief shall not be deemed a waiver of the agreement to arbitrate other disputes. The Parties will use commercially reasonable efforts to notify the other Party and meet-and-confer prior to seeking emergency court relief, except where notice would cause irreparable harm or is impracticable."

Governing law / venue options:
- Option A (Redwood preference): "This Agreement is governed by the laws of the State of California, without regard to conflict of laws rules. Venue for any court action (including actions for provisional relief) shall be in the state or federal courts located in San Francisco County, California, unless the parties agree otherwise in writing."
- Option B (compromise): "This Agreement is governed by the laws of the State of New York. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the Parties agree that actions seeking provisional, injunctive, or other emergency relief may be brought in any court of competent jurisdiction."

Recommendation: Offer Option B as a commercial concession with a clean carveout paragraph above. It meets Meridian's preference while preserving our ability to insist arbitration for the broader dispute and allows court filings for emergency relief where necessary.

Karthik — if we go with Option B, suggest a nominal concession (first-year credit of 5%) and a 60-day SLA uplift for incident response during first 12 months; Marcus, confirm this doesn't create downstream revenue recognition complications.

If agreed, I'll prepare a tracked-change MSA and a short summary for the customer to speed execution.

Laura Bennett
Director, Legal — Contracts
Redwood Inference
